title: Dante Security exits stealth with $10M to make AI agents accountable
excerpt: Dante Security has raised $10mn led by NFX to trace workplace AI agents and assign each one a human owner, after finding agents can be tricked by webpages.
content_html:
Dante Security has come out of stealth with $10M in seed funding to answer a simple question: when an AI agent does something risky at work, who is responsible? NFX led the round, joined by Alpha Drive, Inovia, and other private investors.

The Tel Aviv and New York company goes after a growing blind spot. AI agents act with the valid credentials of real employees, so when one does something risky, it looks approved, and existing security tools let it pass.

Dante’s platform starts by finding the agents running across a company’s systems, including ones that never got security or spending sign-off. It then traces what each agent was told to do, what it actually did, and which systems and data it touched.

Every agent also gets a named human owner, and employees and executives can see their own agents, while security teams keep watch over all of them and set the rules.

The launch comes with some unsettling homework, as the company tested agents from Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, and xAI. It says they could be steered into tasks they would normally refuse, because they treated faked web pages as real permission.

In the same experiment, Dante says its platform pieced together what the agents had done, tied it to the person responsible, and named the right contact to call.

“Security has spent decades deciding who gets the keys,” said co-founder and CEO Moshe Lipsker, who argues accountability is what makes enterprise AI adoption safe at scale.

Lipsker ran Imperva’s Israel operation and global product development until the security firm folded into Thales, and co-founder Gabi Beyo is an Imperva veteran too. Serial entrepreneur Shai Feinberg completes the founding trio.

Dante is less than a year old, and the company says its first paying customers are already coming on board.
